items.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: That’s why Jack DeJohnette is one of my favorite drummers and has been a mentor to me over the years

ctx.x: Was he — gosh I guess I read near the end of his life he was cantankerous? Is that a fair statement or was he not with you perhaps?

Yeah. Not so much with me. I just found a way to try to pull out the positive energy and you know, him and anybody else that I was around. It’s funny when I listen back to the tape there were definitely some things that were said that I would not have been able to put on the record or really maybe even play for too many people, just, you know, him being a little bitter. You can hear that he was a little bitter, even with what I did put on the record. Because he felt like nobody came to visit him when he was…

that were there for him but he felt like nobody was there for him. And it was really sad to see how he passed as far as his living conditions. You know he had I think not really a nurse but a careperson coming in maybe once a day. I don’t know how long they stayed but it didn’t seem like a very comfortable situation for him.
